title: Shalya Proposes Inviting Kalayavana
story:
The kings had come to Kundina to win Rukmini, and they were going home with nothing. Krishna had carried her off from the swayamvara before any of them could move, and now the defeated suitors gathered one last time in the assembly hall of her father Bhishmaka, restless on their beautiful seats, before scattering to their own kingdoms.

Bhishmaka, well read in the laws of conduct, rose and asked their forgiveness. "You all know the calamity that has befallen the swayamvara," he said. "Forgive me for the fruit that is the outcome of my misconduct." He honored them duly and sent away the monarchs of Central India and of the east, west, and north, who departed delighted. But a circle of kings remained, desirous of listening to the mystery: Jarasandha of Magadha, Sunitha, the energetic Dantavakra, Shalya the king of Soubha, king Mahakurma, Kaishika, the leading kings of the Pravara race, the royal sage Venudari, the king of Kashmir, and the kings of the Deccan.

To them Bhishmaka spoke again, aiming his words at his own son. "Observing the movements of my son, my eyes are agitated with fear. I consider all now as mere boys. Krishna alone is the foremost of beings — the incarnation of glory, the partaker of fame — and he has established his fame and the might of his arms in this land of mortals. Blessed is Devaki, the foremost of damsels, who has conceived as her son the lotus-eyed Krishna, identical with the sum total of beauty, the greatest of all in the three worlds, adored of all the immortals."

When he had spoken, Shalya of Soubha rose and answered in sweet words. "O lord of kings, do not lament for your son. Kshatriyas meet either with success or defeat in battle — that is the inevitable course and the eternal religion of mortals. Save Baladeva and Krishna, what third person can withstand your highly powerful son? When by the might of his arms he handles the Bhargava weapons, difficult of being used even by the celestials, what man is capable of bearing it? This eternal being Krishna is without birth or death. In this land of mortals even the holder of the trident cannot defeat him. Knowing Keshava as Ishana, your son did not engage in fight with him."

Then Shalya paused, and said what he had really come to say. "It is not that there is none who can defeat him." The great sage Gargya, desiring a son, had adored Rudra for twelve years, living on powdered iron and practising dreadful and highly difficult penances. When Shankara, pleased, offered him a boon, Gargya prayed for a son whom the kings of Mathura would not be able to slay, and Rudra granted it. By virtue of that boon, Gargya's son Kalayavana is unslayable by the kings of Mathura in the battlefield — and especially in the city of Mathura itself. Though Krishna is highly powerful amongst the princes of Mathura, if Kalayavana comes to battle and fights with him, he will be able to defeat him. "O kings," Shalya said, "if you accept my words as becoming and sound, send an emissary to the capital of the king of the Yavanas."

The leading kings heard him out and were delighted. "We will do it," they said. Only Jarasandha lost heart, recollecting the words of Brahma. "Alas!" he said. "Formerly, assailed by the fear of a foreign king, all the chiefs, seeking refuge with me, used to get back their lost kingdoms, their servants, their armies and conveyances. Now, on account of their bad feelings towards their lord, they excite me to seek another's shelter, like a damsel coming in contact with a stranger. Alas! Even I, who stand afraid of Krishna —" and there his voice died away.

But the will of the kings prevailed, and the emperor who had once sheltered the princes of the earth sent Shalya of Soubha as his envoy to the capital of the Yavanas.
reflection: Shalya's counsel turns the kings' defeat at the swayamvara into a plan against Krishna, and the plan is clever enough that everyone accepts it at once. It is Jarasandha, the mightiest of them, who recoils — because he understands that calling in an ally is also an admission of fear.
next_story_tease: Shalya of Soubha, dispatched as envoy, set out for the capital of the Yavanas.
hero_scene: Shalya of Soubha standing in Bhishmaka's assembly hall in Kundina, addressing the seated kings while Jarasandha broods on his throne among them, the lamps catching the ornaments of the Deccan kings listening in the shadows.
